gloss: opening of a country (to foreign relations)

forms.label: Past polite
forms.negative: {開国|かいこく}しませんでした

forms.label: ている polite
forms.negative: {開国|かいこく}していません

forms.label: ている past
forms.negative: {開国|かいこく}していなかった

forms.label: ている past polite

forms.negative: {開国|かいこく}していませんでした

forms.label: Conditional たら
forms.negative: {開国|かいこく}しなかったら

definitions.explanation: The act of ending a national policy of isolation and opening diplomatic and trade relations with foreign countries. Most commonly refers to Japan's opening in the 1850s after the arrival of Commodore Perry.

examples.japanese: {日本|にほん}は{幕末|ばくまつ}に{開国|かいこく}した。
examples.english: Japan opened its doors at the end of the Edo period.

examples.japanese: ペリーの{来航|らいこう}が{開国|かいこく}のきっかけとなった。
examples.english: Perry's arrival became the catalyst for the opening of the country.

examples.japanese: {開国|かいこく}によって{西洋|せいよう}の{文化|ぶんか}や{技術|ぎじゅつ}が{一気|いっき}に{流入|りゅうにゅう}した。
examples.english: The opening of the country brought a flood of Western culture and technology.

notes:
Almost always used in the context of Japanese history, specifically the end of the {鎖国|さこく} (national isolation) policy in the 1850s. The opposite is {鎖国|さこく} (closing the country).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {開国|かいこく}する (to open the country)
- {開国|かいこく}を{迫|せま}る (to demand the opening of a country)
- {開国|かいこく}を{求|もと}める (to seek the opening of a country)

ETYMOLOGY:
The debate between {開国|かいこく}{派|は} (pro-opening faction) and {攘夷|じょうい}{派|は} (expel-the-foreigners faction) defined late Edo politics. {開国|かいこく} is now used more broadly to describe any country ending isolation.
